name: Three Actions and a Reaction
summary: During an encounter, you can use three single actions on your turn and one reaction per round when its trigger occurs.
reminders: Free actions cost no action; an activity uses all of its listed actions together.

name: Multiple Attack Penalty
summary: On your turn, the second attack-trait check takes a -5 penalty and the third or later takes -10.
reminders: Agile attacks use -4 and -8 instead. Any attack-trait check counts, and the penalty is based on the weapon used for that attack.

name: Cover
summary: Standard cover gives +2 circumstance to AC, Reflex saves against area effects, and Stealth checks to avoid detection.
reminders: Lesser cover gives +1 to AC only. Greater cover gives +4 to the standard-cover checks; lesser cover alone is not enough to Hide.

name: Wounded
summary: When you lose dying, gain wounded 1 or increase an existing wounded value by 1. If you become dying while wounded, add that wounded value to dying.
reminders: Wounded ends after successful Treat Wounds restores HP, or after you reach full HP and rest for 10 minutes.

name: Treat Wounds
summary: With trained Medicine and a healer's toolkit, spend 10 minutes treating one injured living creature; the usual DC is 15.
reminders: The target is temporarily immune for 1 hour, including the treatment time. A success restores 2d8 HP and removes wounded; a critical failure deals 1d8 damage.

name: Recovery Checks
summary: At the start of each turn while dying, make a flat check with DC 10 plus your dying value.
reminders: Critical success lowers dying by 2; success lowers it by 1; failure raises it by 1; critical failure raises it by 2.

name: Recall Knowledge
summary: Use a relevant skill to ask the GM a question about a topic; the GM sets the DC and resolves the check secretly.
reminders: A success gets an accurate answer. On a critical failure, the GM may give false information or no information.

name: Search (Exploration)
summary: While exploring, Search lets you look carefully for hidden doors, concealed hazards, and similar things.
reminders: You usually move at half speed. When you encounter a hidden feature, the GM makes a free secret Seek check; crowded areas can take longer.

name: Simple DCs
summary: For a task without a level, choose a DC by the proficiency rank that best matches its difficulty: 10, 15, 20, 30, or 40 from untrained through legendary.
reminders: The rank is usually not required to attempt the task. Level-based DCs work better for level-based hazards or high-stakes combat challenges.

name: Monster Darkvision
summary: A monster with darkvision sees in darkness and dim light, but only in black and white.
reminders: Some magical darkness blocks normal darkvision; greater darkvision can see through those forms.
